experiment.title: Can a reviewer talk itself out of its false alarms?
experiment.summary: Every model reviewer we have measured catches about half of 30 real defects but also flags about two-thirds of 30 clean changes. EXP 012 asks whether a second pass by the same model, which must name a concrete failing input for every finding or drop it, brings false alarms down to at most 2 of 30 while still catching at least 12 of 30 defects.
experiment.note: Written, hashed and pushed to a public branch before any counted call. The counted run starts only after that push. Nothing in this record may change afterwards; a later change is a new, dated amendment, published first.

question: A reviewer that flags most clean changes cannot be trusted to block a merge on its own. If the cheapest fix is to make the reviewer check its own alarms, the gap between a useful reviewer and a noisy one is a prompt, not a better model. If self-checking does not cut the alarms, or cuts the real catches with them, the gap needs something else: a different model, a second reviewer, or a narrower question.

model.name: minimax-m3.1-flash
model.provider: Ollama Cloud (https://ollama.com/api/chat), one request per call, no tools, no file access
model.thinking: on (the provider default for think: true)
model.price: free until 2026-10-22 23:59 UTC; list price after that $0.15 per 1M input tokens, $0.60 per 1M output tokens
model.onlyModel: Every counted call in this experiment uses this one model. No other model is called.

corpus.boundary: The 58 diffs come from our private repositories and are not published. Only counts and the sealed hashes below are public. The corpus was assembled on 2026-10-14 for a separate calibration, before this experiment existed.
corpus.seededDefinition: 12 defects from the original corpus plus 18 harvested from the review record: a defect raised on a change, the named file changed after it, and a later approval.
corpus.cleanDefinition: Merged changes with no later fix to the same file.

arms.name: Single review (baseline)
arms.procedure: One call with review-prompt.txt. The verdict and findings are used as given.
arms.data: ALREADY MEASURED before this record, disclosed: two runs on 2026-10-21 on the same corpus, model and engine. Defects caught 16 and 16 of 30; false alarms 21 and 19 of 30. A0 is not re-run.

arms.name: Review, then verify
arms.procedure: Pass 1 is exactly A0. When pass 1 is not SHIP and lists findings, pass 2 sends the same model the change description, the diff and the numbered findings with verify-prompt.txt. A finding survives only if pass 2 keeps it with a non-empty failing input. The final verdict is the pass-1 verdict with the surviving findings; if none survive it is SHIP.

review.note: Placeholders: __CHANGE__ is the change description, __DIFF__ the diff.

verify.note: Placeholders: __CHANGE__, __DIFF__, and __FINDINGS__ (one line per finding: number, severity, file, note).

scoring.scorer: The existing review-recall scorer, unchanged. A defect is caught when the verdict is not SHIP and a finding names the defect's file (plus the sealed pattern for the two shared-diff pairs). A false alarm is a clean change given a verdict other than SHIP.
scoring.noVerdict: A pass-1 timeout, transport error or unparseable reply after one retry counts as FIX-NEEDED with no findings: a miss on a defect and a false alarm on a clean change. It is also reported separately.
scoring.verifyFailure: If pass 2 fails after one retry (transport error, another model in the receipt, unparseable reply), the pass-1 result stands unchanged. The alarm is never dropped by a failure. The count of verify failures is reported.

decision.earnsItsKeep: In BOTH A1 runs: false alarms at most 2 of 30 AND defects caught at least 12 of 30.
decision.partial: Not earnsItsKeep, but in both A1 runs false alarms at most 12 of 30 (at least 8 fewer than the A0 mean of 20) AND defects caught at least 12 of 30.
decision.no: Anything else. This includes cutting false alarms by also cutting catches below 12.
decision.why12: 12 of 30 is the lowest recall any measured seat reached on P1 in the earlier calibration. A reviewer below it is no longer competitive on catches.

secondary: Per case, A1 against each A0 run: false alarms removed, catches lost.
How many pass-1 findings pass 2 kept and dropped.
Catches on the 12 original seeds versus the 18 harvested ones (harvested may be inflated, as the calibration noted).
Cost per review at list price and median latency.

spend.bound: Free during the run. At list price the bound is about $2 per 58-change run; the harness accounting cap is $60 per run because a failed call with no billed tokens is priced at a $9 placeholder.
spend.stop: If the free period ends before both A1 runs finish, the run stops and the experiment is published as incomplete, with the finished count. Nothing is extrapolated.

notBefore: The first counted call is made after this record is pushed to a public branch of odin-labs-ai/odin-rnd. The push time is the freeze time.
limits: One model, one corpus, two runs. The a and b runs replay the same 60 cases, so they are not independent samples.
The corpus is private. Readers can check the hashes and the method but cannot rerun the cases.
The verifier is the same model as the reviewer. A different verifier is a different experiment.
Latency depends on shared provider load and is reported, not judged.

privateAdapter.note: The pass-1 seat is our private review-recall adapter (tool-free ollama-chat engine), byte-frozen for this run. Published here as hashes only.

runner.smoke: The runner was exercised once on a synthetic one-function diff that is not in the corpus (pass 1 found the planted bug, pass 2 kept it). No corpus case has been run through A1.
